snippet.description:
So we've previously established how good of an item Manamune/Muramana is. It felt good on Twitch, but what about on Ashe? Can this logic be applied to all Marksmen...?

-Muramana's damage is mostly front-loaded because the on-hit damage is dependent on current mana. The on-hit damage on the main target is "reduced" when hitting multiple targets with Runaan's (mana consumption).

-These tests may not necessarily be accurate of the typical fighting conditions. And some of these builds aren't designed to be used as such. (ER / CDR based builds are more poke- and teamplay oriented as opposed to being aa focused)

-The only relevant runes used were listed. All others weren't active (Legend: Bloodline, Last Stand, Waterwalking, Nimbus Cloak)

-The damage test consisted only of basic attacks, starting from out of combat . Q was used, W was not. 

-BotrK, having the lowest AD gain from any of the full items, will deal significantly less Volley (W) damage. This was not accounted for, since it wasn't used. Trinity Force sheen proc was also only triggered once. 

-No, Ashe Q does not trigger additional instances of On-hit effects such as botrk or muramana. The onhit is applied only to the first of the five shots during the Q uptime.

Interesting interaction with Twitch, specifically: His R hits and Runaan bolts both apply the Muramana on-hit separately. Meaning you can effectively hit up to 2 targets with two instances of Muramana per basic attack (4 if you go Guinsoo's Rageblade).
